free_tier.stated: Notebooks: '20 Gigabytes of auto-saved disk space (/kaggle/working)' per notebook version. Datasets: '200GB per dataset limit', '200GB max private datasets' — the 200 GB private cap is the only account-level storage number published; public datasets are capped per-dataset, not per-account.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: Notebook output survives session end as a versioned artifact — the closest thing here to real object storage — but it is write-once per version, and you cannot run a listener (no inbound ports, no server).

egress.terms: Public dataset/notebook downloads are served without auth and without a published egress meter.

tooling: `kaggle` CLI + REST API (`/api/v1/datasets/download/...`, `/api/v1/kernels/output/...`); `kagglehub` Python client. No rclone backend, but the CLI is scriptable and gsutil-style uploads work through the API.
chaining: 20 GB per notebook output x unlimited notebook versions (each version is an immutable snapshot, addressable and re-mountable as 'Input' in another notebook) => effectively hundreds of GB per account. Plus unlimited public datasets at 200 GB each. Both layers multiply by N free accounts.
limits_note: 12 h session for CPU/GPU notebooks, 9 h for TPU; output only auto-saves to /kaggle/working when you 'Save & Run All'; scratch space outside /kaggle/working dies with the session; 50 top-level files per dataset.
